answer.title: How it answers
answer.reply.stream: Live: the answer as it is written
answer.replyHelp: Progress and Live show one working message, and the answer replaces it. On a platform with drafts, Live shows a private chat a draft instead, and the answer follows it. A long answer goes on in new messages.
answer.conversationHelp: Send /new (or !new) in the app to start a new chat.
answer.conversation.chat: One chat per group or channel
answer.conversation.window: Per person, new after a quiet time
answer.conversation.thread: New chat per message; replies go on
answer.windowRange: Use a whole number from 1 to {{max}}.
answer.languageHelp: The notes the bot writes itself, like confirmations and refusals. The answers of the model follow the language of the conversation.
answer.language.auto: Automatic (your interface language, else the language of the sender)
answer.files: Send the files the agent makes
aside.title: How it works
aside.step1: Give the connection a name and its token. The token is sealed and never shown again.
aside.step2: Pick the agent that answers. It needs a model.
aside.step3: Choose who may write to it, and how it answers.
aside.testText: When you save a new token, LocalAI checks it and names the account it belongs to. Use Test on a saved row to check it again.
answer.filesHelp: After the answer, up to 5 files. Programs and scripts are not sent. The size limit is under Files.
approval.title: Timers and triggers from the chat
approval.help: When the agent sets up something that runs later ("in 10 minutes", "every day"), every run is one model run.
approval.mode.ask: Ask me: the bot proposes it in the chat and the person answers yes or no
approval.mode.auto: Set it up at once and tell the person how to cancel it
approval.mode.auto_readonly: At once when the runs only read and report; otherwise ask
approval.limitsHelp: These limits bound what is set up without asking. Leave a field empty for its default. Anything over a limit is asked instead.
approval.max_pending: Most timers and triggers at once
approval.min_gap_minutes: Fewest minutes between runs of a recurring trigger
approval.max_runs_per_day: Most runs a day, all together
approval.invalid: Use a whole number from 1 to {{max}}, or leave it empty.
approval.acts.title: Runs may act
approval.acts.help: Off: the runs of a trigger made from this chat only read and report. On: they may also do what you tick below, and only what the agent has.
approval.acts.modes: Ask me: you always decide. At once: only when you are paired as sender and every act is ticked here.
approval.acts.act.files: Write files in the agent's folders
approval.acts.act.files.effect: A run can create and change files the agent keeps.
approval.acts.act.addons: Use the actions of the agent's add-ons
approval.acts.act.addons.effect: A run can use what the add-ons of the agent do, including commands.
approval.acts.act.send: Send messages beyond where it reports
approval.acts.act.send.effect: A run can write to other chats and channels on its own.
approval.acts.act.spend: Use paid or external tools and the network
approval.acts.act.spend.effect: A run can call services outside LocalAI, which may cost money.
approval.acts.lacks: The agent does not have this.
files.title: Files
files.help: Leave a field empty to use the limit of the add-on. Your limit can only be lower than that.
files.receiveLabel: Largest file it reads, in MiB
files.sendLabel: Largest file it sends, in MiB
files.tooHigh: The add-on allows at most {{max}} here.
files.receiveHelp: Files that people send to the bot. A bigger file is refused, and the bot says which limit it hit.
files.sendHelp: Files that the agent makes and the bot sends back. A bigger file is not sent, and the bot says which limit it hit.
files.addon.off: This add-on does not move files in this direction, so there is nothing to set.
files.addon.open: The add-on declares no limit, so the limit of the platform applies.
files.host: No bot can move a file above {{max}}. An administrator sets this in the settings.
perm.title: What senders may do
perm.help: Choose what the people who write to this bot may ask the agent to do. Anything switched off stays off for everyone, whatever a role or a pairing says.
perm.noCapsTitle: No permission is on, so these features are off
perm.noCapsText: This bot was saved before permissions existed, or no permission was chosen yet. Until you turn some on, senders cannot send files to the agent, set up triggers, save to memory or have the agent post to a channel. Messages are still answered.
perm.usualHelp: Switches on the everyday permissions that stay inside LocalAI: {{names}}. Sensitive ones are never included.
perm.usualDone: The usual permissions are on. Save to keep them.
perm.usualSaved: The usual permissions are saved for {{name}}.
perm.usualSetHelp: Ticks the everyday permissions that stay inside LocalAI, for what the agent has. Sensitive ones are never included.
perm.sameAsHelp: Copies the permissions the agent has now, sensitive ones too. It is a copy of today and does not follow later changes to the agent.
perm.block.unreadable: The permissions of this agent could not be read.
perm.block.nothing: This agent has no permission that a connection can use.
perm.usualNone: Nothing new to tick: the usual permissions the agent has are already on.
perm.usualSkipped: Not ticked, because the agent does not have them: {{names}}.
perm.sameTicked: Copied {{count}} permissions of {{agent}}: {{names}}. This is a copy of today and does not follow later changes to the agent. Save to keep them.
perm.agentLacks: The agent does not have this.
perm.confirmText: The agent has these sensitive permissions. Once they are on, a sender you paired could use them through this bot:
perm.rule: People on the allowlist can use the ticked permissions. Sensitive ones also need the person to be paired.
perm.stuckTitle: Sensitive permissions are ticked, but nobody is paired
perm.stuckText: A sensitive permission works only for a person you paired with this bot. Until you pair someone, no sender can use: {{names}}.
perm.channelOnlyText: Members of a channel are not trusted one by one, so they cannot use the ticked permissions. Add their user to the allowed people, or set the channel to Let everyone here ask for actions.
perm.sensitiveHelp: Sensitive. Never given to a role. Only a sender you paired can use it, and every use is recorded.
perm.capsHelp: The ceiling for everyone. A role can be given less, never more.
perm.rolesHelp: The platform tells the host which roles a sender has. Choose what each role may do. Sensitive permissions are never given to a role, and a role can only get a permission that is switched on above.
perm.rolesNone: Switch on a permission above that this add-on can give to a role, and it shows here.
perm.channelsHelp: Channels the agent may post to when an allowed person asks, besides the chat where it replies. This does not decide who the bot listens to: see Channels where the bot listens. At most {{max}}.
perm.channelsOff: Switch on "Post to other channels" above to choose where it may post.
perm.channelIdHelp: The ID the platform gives the chat. No spaces.
perm.channelLabelHelp: A name for you and the agent. Optional.
perm.channelApprovedHelp: On: the agent may post here when any allowed person asks. Off: it needs a paired person for each message. This is about posting only, not about who may talk to the bot.
perm.channelProblem.id: Each channel needs an ID of 1 to {{max}} bytes, with no space.
perm.channelProblem.label: A name has at most {{max}} characters.
perm.triggersNeed: Turn on Propose triggers to use this.
pair.title: Paired senders
pair.help: A paired sender proved that they control an allowed account. Only a paired sender can use the sensitive permissions. At most {{max}}; a pairing ends after {{days}} days.
pair.startHelp: Makes a code. Send it to the bot as a direct message from the account to pair, within ten minutes. The code works once.
pair.needSave: Save this bot first, then pair a sender.
pair.codeHelp: Send this code to the bot as a direct message from the account to pair. It is shown only now, works once and expires at {{time}}.
pair.codeGone: The code expired. Make a new one if the sender is not listed yet.
pair.full: Three senders are paired. Remove one to pair another.
access.title: Latest decisions
access.needSave: Save this bot first to see its latest decisions.
access.recentHelp: The latest checks of this server, newest first. They hold IDs and names of permissions, never message text. They reset when the server restarts.
can.title: What this bot can do
can.help: The check the host runs for each message, run on this form as it is now. It changes nothing. A blocked row shows the first problem; more may follow it.
can.sender.listed: A person on the allowed list
can.sender.channel_member: A member of an allowed channel
can.sender.anyone: Anyone who writes to the bot
can.fromForm: Computed from the form as it is now. Save to keep these settings.
can.fromFormNew: Not saved yet. Computed from the form as it is now.
can.loading: Checking what this bot can do
can.errorTitle: Could not check what this bot can do
can.via.allowlist: because this person is on the allowed list
can.via.agentConnection: because this person is paired and the agent is connected to the add-on
can.noPerson: No person is on the allowed list yet. This is what a listed person would get.
can.then.tools: the Tools switch of the agent
ready.title: Readiness
ready.help: What has to be in place for this bot to work, for the form as it is now.
ready.checkingSummary: Checking what the form will do.
ready.unchecked: Could not check this. See "What this bot can do" below.
ready.token.missing: Paste the token of the bot. Without it nothing is received.
ready.token.newTyped: The token is checked with the platform when you save.
ready.token.typed: The new token is checked with the platform when you save.
ready.token.saved: A token is saved. The platform accepted it when it was saved.
ready.agent.credentialsOnly: No agent. This connection only holds the credentials and answers no message.
ready.agent.gone: The chosen agent is not in your list any more. Choose another.
ready.agent.noModel: {{name}} has no model, so it cannot answer. Give it one.
ready.who.anyone: Anyone who can message the bot may use it.
ready.who.nobody: Nobody is allowed yet, so the bot ignores every message. Add a person.
ready.who.channelsOnly: Only channels are on the list. People in a channel can chat, but they can use the ticked permissions only where the channel is set to Let everyone here ask for actions.
ready.who.mixed: {{count}} entries are allowed, people and channels.
ready.perm.none: No permission is on. Senders can chat, and nothing else.
ready.perm.noneSaved: No permission is on, so files, memory, triggers and posts are off.
ready.perm.onlyOwnRows: The other permissions are off. Triggers and files are below.
ready.perm.ok_one: {{count}} permission is on and a sender can use it.
ready.perm.ok_other: {{count}} permissions are on and a sender can use them.
ready.perm.dead_other: Nobody can use {{count}} of the permissions that are on: {{names}}. First: {{message}}
ready.addons.off: The agent has the {{addon}} tools {{tools}}, and it cannot use them in this chat until you turn on "{{permission}}".
ready.addons.blocked: The agent has the {{addon}} tools {{tools}}, and they are held back. {{message}}
ready.addons.ok: The agent can use the {{addon}} tools {{tools}} in this chat.
ready.addons.paired: Paired people can use the {{addon}} write tools {{tools}} in this chat, because this agent is connected to {{connection}} (write mode: {{mode}}). People who are not paired need "{{permission}}".
ready.addons.removed: You turned off "{{permission}}", so nobody can use the {{addon}} write tools {{tools}} in this chat, not even paired people. Turn it on to bring them back; people on the allowlist who are not paired get them too.
ready.addons.modeOff: The agent has the {{addon}} write tools {{tools}}, and they are held back because the write mode of {{connection}} is off. Change the write mode on that connection.
ready.triggers.off: The agent cannot set reminders or scheduled tasks here.
ready.triggers.blocked: Triggers are on, and they cannot be used. {{message}}
ready.triggers.ok.ask: The agent can propose triggers. You confirm each one before it starts.
ready.triggers.ok.auto: The agent can propose triggers. They start at once, without asking you.
ready.triggers.ok.auto_readonly: The agent can propose triggers. A trigger that only reads starts at once; you confirm any other.
ready.files.offReceive: Senders cannot send files to the agent.
ready.files.offBoth: Senders cannot send files to the agent, and the bot sends none back.
ready.files.blocked: Receiving files is on, and it cannot be used. {{message}}
ready.files.ok: Senders can send files to the agent, and the bot can send files back.
ready.files.okReceive: Senders can send files to the agent. The bot sends none back.
ready.notify.off: No chat gets notices from this bot.
agentOptionalHint: Optional. Without an agent this connection only holds the token, the repository list and the write mode for your chats. It answers no messages. Choose an agent to let it listen.
ready.blocker.nobodyPaired: This needs a person you paired with the bot, and nobody is paired yet.
approvals.title: Runs without asking
approvals.help: Some tools of this add-on can run without a confirmation card, but only when the owner chose that on the page of the add-on. Every other tool and every other sender is still asked.
approvals.state.idle: Set to run without asking, does nothing now
approvals.line.asks: A card waits for the owner's OK.
approvals.line.runs: For the owner's own chats and for senders paired with the bot. Everyone else is still asked.
approvals.line.idle: The write mode of this connection is Read only, so no write tool runs.
approvals.line.other: Only the owner and a paired sender skip the card. This kind of sender is asked.
dup.text: This bot is also connected as {{name}}. Both connections will answer the same message.
dup.confirmHelp: Save it anyway only if you want to get two answers to each message.
access.noteSave.title: Notes
access.noteSave.now: Saves notes at once and tells you, with an Undo
access.noteSave.ask: Notes from this kind of sender wait for the owner
trust.title: Channels where the bot listens
trust.help: For each channel on the allowed list, choose what the people who write there may do. This is not the list of channels the bot posts to.
trust.act: Let everyone here ask for actions
trust.switch: Let everyone in {{channel}} ask for actions
trust.consequence.act: Anyone who can post here can make the bot read their files, set reminders and use the other everyday actions you allowed. Sensitive things still need pairing.
trust.consequence.answer: The bot answers here, but only people on the allowed list can ask for actions.
trust.emptyCeiling: No permission is ticked on this connection, so files and other actions are still refused for everyone.
ready.channelTrust.act: People in {{channels}} can ask for everyday actions. Sensitive ones still need pairing.
ready.channelTrust.answer: People in {{channels}} cannot use actions: set it to Let everyone here ask for actions.
ready.channelTrust.noCaps: Nothing is ticked under permissions, so files and other actions are refused even where everyone may ask.
can.sender.channel_acts: A member of a channel set to Let everyone here ask for actions
can.via.channel: Everyone in this channel can ask for this because the channel is set to Let everyone here ask for actions
ready.postTo_one: The bot may post to 1 other channel when an allowed person asks. That does not trust the people in it.
ready.postTo_other: The bot may post to {{count}} other channels when an allowed person asks. That does not trust the people in them.
access.toolsHelp: The latest calls of add-on tools that used this connection or came in through this bot, newest first, at most 20. They hold tool names and reasons, never what was asked or answered. They reset when the server restarts.
